security_audit.summary: Most Ruby backtick findings are false positives from Markdown fences or TypeScript template literals. The real risks are documented shell commands that run unpinned npx packages, register an MCP server, and access hidden SQLite memory databases. No prompt injection text was found in SKILL.md.

remediation.suggestion: Pin AgentDB package versions and verify package provenance before recommending npx commands or MCP registration.
Warn users before creating .agentdb or reading .swarm memory databases, and document cleanup steps.
Add guidance to redact secrets from trajectories before export, import, migration, or verbose logging.

semantic_findings.title: Unpinned Remote CLI and MCP Registration
semantic_findings.description: The quick start instructs users to run npx agentdb@latest and register an MCP server with claude mcp add. This can execute changing package code and persist a local tool integration.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The commands are explicit and use @latest with MCP registration. The risk is supply-chain exposure and persistent tool configuration.

semantic_findings.title: Persistent Storage of Agent Queries and Trajectories
semantic_findings.description: Examples store user queries, task trajectories, outcomes, metrics, and distilled patterns in a local ReasoningBank database. This can retain sensitive project context if users do not redact inputs.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The examples directly store query text, trajectory steps, outcomes, and metrics. Sensitive content risk depends on what users record.

semantic_findings.title: Memory Export Can Expose Reasoning Data
semantic_findings.description: CLI operations export .agentdb/reasoningbank.db to backup.json and enable verbose migration logs. These outputs may expose stored trajectories or memory metadata.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The export and verbose migration commands are documented. The exact sensitivity depends on the stored ReasoningBank data.

content.user_title: Build Adaptive Agent Memory with AgentDB
content.value_statement: Agents often lose useful lessons after each task. This skill guides ReasoningBank memory, verdict judgment, and pattern retrieval with AgentDB.
actual_capabilities: Initializes an AgentDB-backed ReasoningBank database through documented CLI commands.
Shows how to store trajectories, experiences, verdicts, and distilled patterns.
Demonstrates retrieval with similarity search, MMR, and context synthesis.
Explains migration from legacy ReasoningBank memory stores.
Covers database export, import, statistics, and troubleshooting commands.
limitations: Requires Node.js 18 and the external AgentDB package.
Examples assume embeddings are available from the surrounding application.
Does not provide production access controls or data retention policies.
Performance claims depend on workload, hardware, and AgentDB configuration.

use_cases.title: Improve Coding Agents
use_cases.description: Use stored trajectories to help agents reuse successful debugging and optimization patterns.

use_cases.title: Migrate Legacy Memory
use_cases.description: Move ReasoningBank data from legacy SQLite storage into an AgentDB-backed workflow.

use_cases.title: Evaluate Agent Outcomes
use_cases.description: Compare new trajectories with past successful patterns before accepting an agent decision.

prompt_templates.title: Set Up ReasoningBank
prompt_templates.prompt: Guide me through setting up ReasoningBank with AgentDB for a local coding agent. Include prerequisites and safety checks.

prompt_templates.title: Store a Successful Experience
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me design a ReasoningBank entry for this completed task. Include domain, confidence, metrics, and retrieval notes.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a Legacy Migration
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a migration plan from legacy ReasoningBank memory to AgentDB. Include validation, backup, rollback, and privacy checks.

prompt_templates.title: Design Adaptive Retrieval
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a retrieval strategy using similarity search, MMR, context synthesis, and memory optimization for a multi-domain agent.

output_examples.input: A developer asks how to remember successful API optimization work.
output: Capture the task, steps, outcome, latency metrics, and confidence score.
Retrieve similar patterns before future endpoint changes.

output_examples.input: A platform engineer wants to move old memory data to AgentDB.
output: Start with a backup of the legacy memory database.
Run migration in a test workspace before production use.
Validate counts, domains, confidence ranges, and retrieval quality.

output_examples.input: A research team wants to judge new agent decisions.
output: Compare the trajectory with past successful patterns.
Check similarity, sample size, confidence, and failure history.
Mark uncertain outcomes for review instead of automatic acceptance.

best_practices: Pin package versions before running CLI commands in shared environments.
Review stored trajectories for secrets before export or migration.
Use domains and confidence thresholds to limit irrelevant memories.
anti_patterns: Do not store raw credentials, private prompts, or customer data in memory patterns.
Do not run unpinned remote commands in privileged workspaces.
Do not treat high similarity as proof that an outcome is correct.

faq.question: Does this skill install AgentDB automatically?
faq.answer: No. It documents CLI and API patterns; users choose when to run commands.

faq.question: Can it work with Claude Code?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes MCP setup concepts for Claude Code and AgentDB integration.

faq.question: Can I use it with Codex?
faq.answer: Yes. The guidance is tool-agnostic and can support Codex workflows that manage agent memory.

faq.question: Does it require a network connection?
faq.answer: Package installation and documentation links may need network access. Local database operations can run offline after setup.

faq.question: Where is memory stored?
faq.answer: Examples use SQLite database files under hidden workspace directories such as .agentdb and .swarm.

faq.question: Is stored memory private by default?
faq.answer: It stays local in these examples, but exports and migrations can expose sensitive task data.
